title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche sequel. Grothendieck is analysing profinite groups attached to the two elliptic generators rho and sigma, which play the role of the order-6 and order-4 elements of SL2(Z)^ with rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1. The groups involved are:
- S_0^Pi Gamma^!_{rho,sigma}: a group of triples u = (u,a,b), where u lies in a hatted group Z^ (probably a normaliser or centraliser) and a, b lie in the normalisers N^x_rho, N^x_sigma. The triples are subject to the congruences (87): u = b mod Pi_0^ and u = eps_3[sigma] a mod Pi^, with Pi_0 a subgroup of Pi.
- Z^!_{rho,sigma} = M[0]: the quotient group. It carries two sign characters eps_3 and eps_2 with values in mu = {+-1}.
- L_rho, L_sigma: the cyclic groups generated by rho and sigma.

What the previous page established.
- S_0^{Pi_0}Gamma^{!o} is a distinguished subgroup of index 8 in S_0^Pi Gamma^!.
- S_0^Pi Gamma^! is an extension of Z^! by mu.
- This extension is pulled back, along (eps_3, eps_2): Z^! -> mu x mu, from the order-8 central extension (84): 1 -> mu -> E -> mu x mu -> 1, where E = S_0^Pi Gamma / S_0^{Pi_0}Gamma^o.

What this page does.
- Diagram (85) has three rows:
  - top: E as an extension of mu x mu by mu;
  - middle: S_0^Pi Gamma^! as an extension of Z^! by mu;
  - bottom: S_0 Gamma^! as an extension of Z^! by L_rho x L_sigma.
- The point stated (86) is Baer functoriality of Ext. The extension class is contravariant in the quotient and covariant in the kernel. So:
  - pulling E back along (eps_3, eps_2) gives the middle row;
  - pushing the middle row forward along the 'diagonal' map mu -> L_rho x L_sigma, -1 |-> (rho^3, sigma^2), gives the bottom row.
- Thus the large extension of Z^! by L_rho x L_sigma is entirely encoded in one class in H^2(mu x mu, mu) (with trivial action), together with two sign characters and the identification -1 = rho^3 = sigma^2.

The question. Grothendieck then asks for the isomorphism type of E. Since E is a central extension of a Klein group by mu, x^2 lies in mu for every x, so element orders divide 4. Are they all at most 2? He writes u^2 = (u^2, a^2, b^2), notes it lies in S_0^Pi Gamma^{!o}, and asks whether it lies in S_0^{Pi_0}Gamma^{!o}.

The answer, on the next page.
- x^2 = 1 iff eps_3(x) = 1 or eps_2(x)eps_3(x) = 1, i.e. x lies in E' union E'''.
- These are two of the three order-4 preimages of the index-2 subgroups of mu x mu. Their union has 6 elements.
- So E has 6 solutions of x^2 = 1 and two elements of order 4 (those with eps_3 = -1, eps_2 = 1). Hence E is dihedral of order 8.
- This matches the previous page: E' and E''' are the two Klein four-subgroups, the splittings over Z^!' and Z^!''' that are not normal, while the third preimage is cyclic of order 4.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim that element orders divide 4 is immediate, since x^2 lies in the central mu for an extension of an elementary abelian 2-group.
Not fully determinable from this page: the eventual conclusion (next page) only gives the set of involutions. Grothendieck does not explicitly name E as D_4 here, though the count forces it.

ideas.what: Encoding the extension of Z^! by L_rho x L_sigma via a single order-8 central extension of mu x mu by mu, using pullback along sign characters and pushout along mu -> L_rho x L_sigma, -1 |-> (rho^3, sigma^2)
ideas.modern_name: Baer functoriality of Ext / H^2; reduction of an extension class to a class in H^2(Klein group, Z/2)

ideas.what: Identification of the central element -1 with rho^3 = sigma^2 (the 'diagonal homomorphism') in profinite SL2-type groups attached to the elliptic generators
ideas.modern_name: Center of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 (amalgam over -1); profinite analogue
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in La Longue Marche (1981) discussions of SL2(Z)^ and elliptic elements

ideas.what: Determining the group of order 8 by counting solutions of x^2 = 1 in terms of sign characters eps_3, eps_2
ideas.modern_name: Classification of central extensions of (Z/2)^2 by Z/2 (D_4 vs Q_8 vs abelian) via the associated quadratic form

missed.claim: The extension of the 'lacets' data by mu is shown to be governed by a dihedral D_4 class pulled back via the sign characters (eps_3, eps_2). The margin question on the previous page, whether there is an algebraic/automorphic section of the extension restricting to the given ones on the sub-pieces, is left open. Relating this sign/2-torsion obstruction to known sign subtleties in the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (e.g. the lambda and +-1 issues in the action on SL2(Z)^) is not done in the literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: L'intérêt de (84) est qu'elle permet de récupérer l'extension ... par les lois covariante-contravariantes dans le foncteur "extensions"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This might matter for a careful treatment of 2-torsion and sign issues in GT^ acting on SL2(Z)^ and on the genus-1 Teichmüller tower. However, the computation itself is elementary, and its relevance is speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine homological bookkeeping step inside a long unpublished computation. The pullback/pushout reduction of the extension and the order count in a group of order 8 are standard. The interest is only in the context (Grothendieck's own working-out of the 'équation des lacets'), not in a new result.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed as '∫_0^π' is Grothendieck's hatted S notation \hat S_0^{Π} (as on the previous page): read \hat S_0^Π Γ_{ρ,σ}, \hat S_0^{Π_0}Γ^o_{ρ,σ}, \hat S_0 Γ^!_{ρ,σ}.
Below (84) the vertical sign under ℰ is '≃' (written rotated): ℰ ≃ \hat S_0^Π Γ_{ρ,σ} / \hat S_0^{Π_0} Γ^o_{ρ,σ}.

In diagram (85), the arrows from the middle row to the bottom row are downward inclusions (hooked arrows): μ ↪ L_ρ×L_σ and \hat S_0^Π Γ^! ↪ \hat S_0 Γ^!. The right column has Z^! = Z^! (a vertical equality with arrows). The arrows from the middle row to the top row point upward: the identity on μ, a map to ℰ, and (ε_3,ε_2).

In (87) the hats under u, a, b indicate u ∈ \hat Z, a ∈ \hat N^×_ρ, b ∈ \hat N^×_σ, which the margin NB explains. The margin note reads roughly: 'NB Pour introduction des congruences, u=(u,a,b), écrire ε_3[σ], ε_3[τ'] etc plutôt que ε_3(σ), ε_3(τ') etc, pour σ, τ' ...'.
The last line reads: u^2 = (u^2, a^2, b^2) ∈ \hat S_0^{Π} Γ^{!o}.
